content.text:
This confirms the `disableExpiredAlarms()` method (iterating `set` and calling `enable()`, which mutates `set` via `changeAlarm`) persisted unchanged from `e86f6cf` (a rename-only commit from `AlarmsManager` to `Alarms`) all the way through `717ab02`, until finally fixed in `62dd6a1`. The root logic was introduced in `f1939c88`.

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: f1939c88e3f8602b993b1b2e30bda8b4adb34409

## Reasoning

**(1) Investigation:** I traced the history of `Alarms.java` (originally `AlarmsManager.java`) using `git log -p`, searching for the introduction of `changeAlarm`, `setNextAlert`, the `set` field, and the `for (Alarm alarm : set)` loop that the fix commit (`62dd6a1`) rewrites. I then checked each intermediate commit touching this file to see when the problematic pattern first appeared and whether it was altered before the fix.

**(2) Root cause:** Commit `f1939c88` is where the class first introduced an in-memory `Set<Alarm> set` field as a live cache of alarms (previously alarms were always re-read from a `Cursor`). In the same commit:
- `changeAlarm(Alarm alarm)` was written to mutate this shared field: `set.remove(alarm); set.add(alarm);`.
- `enable(int id, boolean enable)` was rewritten to call `changeAlarm(alarm)`, thus also mutating `set`.
- `disableExpiredAlarms()` was rewritten to iterate directly over the live field `for (Alarm alarm : set) { ... enable(alarm.getId(), false); ... }`.

This creates a classic `ConcurrentModificationException`: the for-each loop takes an `Iterator` over `set`, and calling `enable()` inside the loop body triggers `set.remove()`/`set.add()` on that same collection, invalidating the iterator mid-iteration.

Before this commit, `disableExpiredAlarms` (and `calculateNextAlert`) built a fresh local `HashSet` from a DB `Cursor` each time and iterated that local copy — calling `enable()` inside that loop was safe because `enable()` only touched the database, not the collection being iterated. `f1939c88` is what first coupled the iteration and the mutation onto the same shared `set` field.

**(3) Supporting evidence:** Walking forward through every subsequent commit that touched this code (`c502083`, `391f995`, `e86f6cf`, `dd67bef`, `e9bf160`, `6f5a4ed`, `506f53e`, `717ab02`), the unsafe pattern — iterating `set` while calling `enable()`/`changeAlarm()` which mutates `set` — is carried forward verbatim (only renamed/relocated, e.g. moved from `disableExpiredAlarms()` into `init()` in `717ab02`). The bug-fixing commit `62dd6a1` directly addresses this by: (a) replacing the `enable()` call inside the loop with direct field mutation + `writeToDb()` (no `set` mutation during iteration), and (b) completely removing `changeAlarm()`'s `set.remove(alarm); set.add(alarm);` mutation, replacing all its callers with a non-mutating `writeToDb()` plus explicit `setNextAlert()`/`notifyAlarmListChangedListeners()` calls. This matches exactly undoing the hazardous pattern first introduced in `f1939c88`.

I'm fairly confident in this attribution since the unsafe pattern is traceable continuously from `f1939c88` to the fix with no intervening commit altering it, but I did not find an actual crash log/stack trace in the repo (none present) to corroborate that a `ConcurrentModificationException` was literally reported — this conclusion is based on static code-path analysis of the collection mutation-during-iteration pattern, which is the standard interpretation this type of fix addresses.
